sentences.text: Gasparinisuchus is distinguished from other peirosaurids by its broad snout and the absence of an antorbital fenestra — the opening in the skull that lies in front of the eye socket.
Features of the referred specimen indicate a tall, broad snout with maxillary teeth implanted in discrete sockets and a convex alveolar edge.
Gasparinisuchus can be differentiated from Peirosaurus by its broad, rounded rostrum, short premaxilla, reduced perinareal fossa, and short interdental spaces.
The genus Gasparinisuchus is known from only two fossil individuals.
The holotype specimen was originally described by Gasparini in 1982 and 1991 under the name Peirosaurus torminni and was discovered at the Loma de la Lata locality in Neuquén Province, Patagonia.
The referred specimen was found at the Área de Cañadón Amarrillo locality in Mendoza Province, Patagonia.

The genus Gasparinisuchus was formally described and named in 2012 by Martinelli, Sertich, Garrido, and Praderio, and the generic name honors the paleontologist Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini for her work on South American crocodyliforms.
The specific name peirosauroides is derived from the genus Peirosaurus and the Greek word for 'shaped', referring to its role in defining the Peirosauridae family.
Gasparinisuchus is classified as a peirosaurid notosuchian.
Gasparinisuchus belongs to the family Peirosauridae.
Gasparinisuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous, from the Santonian to early Campanian stages, in western central Argentina.
Gasparinisuchus lived between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago.

The reclassification of the Argentine specimen as Gasparinisuchus suggests that older Argentine and younger Brazilian Late Cretaceous faunas were mostly distinct, challenging earlier views of a direct link between them.
